issues.display_title: Issue #198: Blue Line save: take the tour key from GoThru, not from the request
issues.main_description_html:
Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Follow-up to #195 (PR #196). Found while checking PRD GoThruMedia/gothru-3d-floormap#1082 against the released code.

Problem

PUT /v1/gothru/tours/:mid/panoramas (UpdatePanoramas, src/action/v1/gothru/proxy.go) checks that the caller owns :mid, then forwards the request body unchanged to GoThru PUT /v1/internal/panoramas/locations/batch with the Internal-API-Key.

GoThru does not use :mid there. BatchUpdatePanoLocationAction resolves the tour from the body's tour_key (getModerationIdByTourKey) and updates 2_lat / 3_lng of the panoramas of that moderation. The internal endpoint has no user, so it cannot check ownership itself.

:mid and tour_key are never compared. A signed-in user who owns any tour can send their own :mid with another tour's tour_key and overwrite that tour's panorama positions. Tour keys are public (https://tourmkr.com/F1{tour_key}), and so are panorama ids (the public panoramas API).

Checked on this repo main 0084e84 and GoThru API main c165c705b. Both editors that save (single tour, and the multiple-tour editor since gothru-3d-floormap#1142) go through this endpoint.

Scope

Take the tour key from GoThru, not from the request.

  1. Replace the ownership read (/v1/panoramas/locations?mid=&limit=1) with one call to the caller's own tour list, made with the caller's GoThru token: GET /v1/tours/list?search=<tour_key from the body>&limit=100. GoThru scopes that list to the caller (user_id) and search matches tour_key.
  2. Find the row whose moderation_id equals :mid. No such row, or a row with an empty tour_key → 404 tour not found, and the internal endpoint is not called.
  3. Forward that row's tour_key to the internal endpoint, with the request's locations. The body's tour_key is a search term only.

The number of GoThru calls stays the same: one read, one write.

Not changing

  • API contract: request and response stay as they are (tour_key is still required in the body). No FE change.
  • GoThru API: no change needed.

Acceptance criteria

  • A request with the caller's :mid and another tour's tour_key answers 404 and never reaches /v1/internal/panoramas/locations/batch.
  • A request with the caller's :mid and its own tour_key is forwarded as before.
  • When the search also matches the :mid row for another reason (search is a LIKE over the name too), the forwarded tour_key is the one GoThru lists for :mid, never the body's.
  • A :mid the caller does not own answers 404, as today.
  • Not connected → 409 gothru_not_connected; GoThru down → 502; both as today.
  • go test ./... passes.

Known limits

  • limit=100: a search that matches more than 100 of the caller's tours can leave the :mid row off the page, and the save answers 404. It refuses; it never writes to the wrong tour.
  • GoThru lists tour_key from 0_moderation, while the internal endpoint looks in hosted_tours.tours first. GoThru writes the same key to both when it creates a hosted tour (addTourData, GetDetailTourMergeAction), so they agree.

RESULT

Implemented and merged to development (8a18148, PR #199). go build ./..., go vet ./... and go test ./... pass.

What changed (src/action/v1/gothru/proxy.go)

  • New ownTourKey(userID, mid, hint): one read of the caller's own tour list with the caller's GoThru token (GET /v1/tours/list?search=<tour_key from the body>&limit=100). It returns the tour_key of the row whose moderation_id equals :mid.
  • UpdatePanoramas forwards that key to PUT /v1/internal/panoramas/locations/batch. The body's tour_key is a search term only. No row for :mid, or a row without a key → 404 tour not found, and the internal endpoint is not called.
  • This replaces the earlier ownership read (/v1/panoramas/locations?mid=&limit=1): still one GoThru read and one write. The API contract is unchanged, so the FE needs nothing.

Tests (src/action/v1/gothru/proxy_test.go)

  • Another tour's key with the caller's :mid → 404, no batch call.
  • A :mid the caller does not own → 404, no batch call.
  • The :mid row found through its name → the forwarded key is GoThru's, not the body's.
  • A tour without a key → 404. Not connected → 409, GoThru not called.
  • Mutation checks: forwarding the body's key, and accepting any listed row, each turn a test red.

Not verified: the fix was not run against the live GoThru API. It relies on the deployed tour list matching tour_key in search (in GoThru's searchModerationIds since 2026-05-07). A 404 on every Blue Line save after deploy would mean the deployed search differs.

Known limit: limit=100. A search matching more than 100 of the caller's tours can miss the :mid row; the save then answers 404 and writes nothing.

Released to main (250db6a, PR #200).

Commit: 77d165d

issues.display_title: Issue #201: Connect, show and disconnect a GoThru account for the signed-in user
issues.main_description_html:
Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Bug report: GoThruMedia/gothru-3d-floormap#1107. PM decisions: GoThruMedia/gothru-3d-floormap#1151. Follow-up to #182 and #188.

Problem

On the Blue Line page, Connect to GoThru Dashboard runs the same flow as Continue with GoThru on the login page: the FE posts the Keycloak access token to POST /v1/auth/keycloak, which is public and resolves the Floormap user from the GoThru identity (link by sub, then verified email, then a new user). It never knows who is signed in, so the answer is a session for that user and the signed-in account is replaced. In #1107 a tester signed in with Google as one account and ended up in another.

There is no way to attach a GoThru account to the account that is already signed in, to see which one is attached, or to detach it.

Decisions (#1151)

  1. Connect attaches the GoThru account to the signed-in Floormap account. Name, email, projects and role do not change.
  2. A GoThru account already attached to another Floormap account is refused.
  3. The Blue Line page shows which GoThru account is connected (its email).
  4. A Disconnect action. To use another GoThru account, the user disconnects and connects again. Nothing is removed in GoThru.
  5. A GoThru email that differs from the Floormap email is allowed.

POST /v1/auth/keycloak (sign-in) stays as it is.

Scope

⚠️ API contract change: three new endpoints under /v1/gothru, behind middleware.Auth(). No migration: user_keycloak_links already holds everything.

GET /v1/gothru/connection

→ 200 { "connected": bool, "email": string }

  • connected: the caller has a usable GoThru token (the same rule the tour proxies use before answering 409 gothru_not_connected).
  • email: the linked GoThru account's email (its username when Keycloak sent no email), "" when there is no link.

POST /v1/gothru/connection, body { "access_token": "<Keycloak access token>" }

Verifies the token exactly as POST /v1/auth/keycloak does (signature, issuer, audience, azp), then:

  • (realm, sub) linked to the caller → refresh the GoThru token.
  • (realm, sub) linked to another user → 409 gothru_account_in_use. Nothing changes.
  • the caller is linked to a different sub → 409 gothru_already_connected (disconnect first).
  • otherwise → create the link for the caller.

Then trade the token for the GoThru API token (gothru.Connect). Unlike at sign-in, this is not best-effort: a failed exchange answers 502 and a link created by this request is removed, so a connect either works or leaves nothing behind.

→ 200 { "connected": true, "email": "…" }

Other errors: 400 missing access_token, 400 invalid GoThru token (not the 401 the sign-in answers: behind a session, 401 means the Floormap session is gone), 502 Keycloak keys unreachable.

No email rule applies here (decision 5): the caller is already signed in to Floormap and the token proves they hold the GoThru account.

DELETE /v1/gothru/connection

Deletes the caller's link row, and the stored GoThru token with it. → 200 { "connected": false, "email": "" }. Idempotent.

  • 409 gothru_sign_in_only when the caller has no password and an unverified email: GoThru is the only way into that account, and without the link the next GoThru sign-in would be refused (the email branch of resolveKeycloakUser needs a verified email).
  • The GoThru account is free afterwards: it can be connected to another Floormap account, or used to sign in.

Behaviour to know

  • A user who signs in with Continue with GoThru is connected again by that sign-in (it creates the link and stores the token, as today). Disconnect lasts until they next sign in with GoThru.
  • User has no marker for Google sign-in, so a user without a password cannot be told apart further than the rule above. A GoThru-created user with a verified email who disconnects is linked again by email at the next GoThru sign-in.

Acceptance criteria

  • Connect with a GoThru account that is not linked: the caller gets the link and the token; the caller's name, email and role are unchanged; no session is issued.
  • Connect with a GoThru account linked to another user → 409 gothru_account_in_use; neither user's link changes.
  • Connect while linked to a different GoThru account → 409 gothru_already_connected.
  • Connect again with the same GoThru account refreshes the token.
  • A failed GoThru exchange → 502, and no link is left from that request.
  • GET reports connected and email for: no link, a link with a usable token, a link with an expired token.
  • Disconnect removes the link; the tour proxies then answer 409 gothru_not_connected; the same GoThru account can be connected by another user.
  • Disconnect is refused for a passwordless user with an unverified email.
  • All three routes need a session (401 without).
  • go test ./... passes.

FE counterpart: a task on GoThruMedia/gothru-3d-floormap (Connect calls the new endpoint instead of signing in again; connected email and Disconnect on the Blue Line page).

RESULT

Implemented and merged to development (a9b29c0, PR #202). go build ./..., go vet ./... and go test ./... pass.

What changed

  • src/action/v1/auth/gothru_connection.go: GetGothruConnection, ConnectGothru, DisconnectGothru. They sit in auth because connect needs verifyKeycloakToken, and auth already imports gothru.
  • src/action/v1/gothru/proxy.go: Connected(userID), the rule the tour proxies already use.
  • src/controllers/v1/gothru/gothru.go and src/routes/v1/gothru.go: GET, POST and DELETE /v1/gothru/connection, behind middleware.Auth(). None issues a session. No migration.

Rules as built

  • Connect: another user's GoThru account → 409 gothru_account_in_use; the caller already has a different one → 409 gothru_already_connected; the same one → token refreshed. A failed GoThru exchange → 502, and a link made by that request is removed.
  • An invalid GoThru token answers 400 here (the sign-in answers 401): behind a session, 401 means the Floormap session is gone.
  • Disconnect removes the link and the token; 409 gothru_sign_in_only for a user with no password and an unverified email.
  • A user who signs in with Continue with GoThru is connected again by that sign-in.

Tests: src/action/v1/auth/gothru_connection_test.go (13 cases, against the fake realm and fake GoThru API of the sign-in tests) and src/routes/v1/gothru_test.go (session required, status codes). Five mutation checks each turn a test red.

Not verified: the real flow through Keycloak and the GoThru API. From outside, without a session, the new routes cannot be told apart from the old build (the /v1/gothru group answers 401 either way).

Released to main (76a32bb, PR #203) on 2026-10-01. FE counterpart: GoThruMedia/gothru-3d-floormap#1152 (PR #1153).

Commit: 2bef435

issues.display_title: Issue #204: Project type: keep Blue Line Map projects apart from floor map projects
issues.main_description_html:
Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

PRD: GoThruMedia/gothru-3d-floormap#1156 (Blue Line Map). PM questions: GoThruMedia/gothru-3d-floormap#1157. This is the part of the PRD that does not wait for those answers.

Problem

PRD #1156 adds a second kind of project: a Blue Line Map (a map of GoThru Blue Line tours), "a separate project type from a 3D project", with its own dashboard.

Today projects has no type. GET /v1/projects and GET /v1/projects/recent return every project of the user, so a Blue Line Map project would show up in the Workspace list and open in the floor plan editor, and the Blue Line Map dashboard could not list its own projects.

Scope

⚠️ API contract change and ⚠️ a new column: run the migration before this is merged (see Deploy).

  1. Column projects.project_type VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'floormap', with a migration file in migrations/. Two values: floormap (every project that exists today) and blue_line_map.
  2. POST /v1/projects accepts an optional projectType. Absent → floormap. Any other value → 400, and nothing is created.
  3. GET /v1/projects and GET /v1/projects/recent accept an optional ?type=.
    • Absent → floormap, so the Workspace keeps listing floor map projects only, with no FE change.
    • ?type=blue_line_map → Blue Line Map projects only.
    • Any other value → 400.
    • status, search and sort keep working together with it.
  4. Every project payload (create, list, recent, get, update, duplicate) carries project_type.
  5. The type is set at creation and never changes. PATCH /v1/projects/:id ignores it, as it ignores every key it does not know. A duplicate keeps the type of its source.

Not in this task: where a Blue Line Map keeps its tours, and what GET /v1/live/:key returns for one. Both depend on answer 3 of #1157.

Deploy

The deploy does not run migrations (DB_AUTO_MIGRATE=false), and a merge to development is already a production deploy. Without the column, GET /v1/projects fails for every user (the query names the column) and no project can be created.

Run the migration first, then merge.

Acceptance criteria

  • A project created without projectType is a floormap; with projectType: "blue_line_map" it is a Blue Line Map; an unknown value answers 400 and creates nothing.
  • GET /v1/projects without type returns floor map projects only; with type=blue_line_map, Blue Line Map projects only; an unknown value answers 400.
  • GET /v1/projects/recent follows the same rule.
  • The status filter and the sort still apply together with type.
  • project_type is in the create, list, recent and get payloads.
  • Duplicating a Blue Line Map project gives a Blue Line Map project.
  • PATCH cannot change the type.
  • go test ./... passes.

FE counterpart: the Blue Line Map dashboard task on GoThruMedia/gothru-3d-floormap, created once #1157 is answered.

RESULT

Implemented and merged to development (bc44da2, PR #207) on 2026-10-02. go build ./..., go vet ./... and go test ./... pass.

What changed

  • src/models/models.go: Project.ProjectType (project_type VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'floormap'), ProjectTypeFloormap, ProjectTypeBlueLineMap, IsValidProjectType.
  • src/action/v1/project/create.go: optional projectType; an unknown value → 400.
  • src/action/v1/project/list.go, recent.go: optional ?type=, read by requestedProjectType. Absent → floormap; an unknown value → 400.
  • src/action/v1/project/shared.go: every project payload carries project_type.
  • migrations/202610020001_add_project_type_to_projects.sql.

As built

  • The Workspace sends no type, so it keeps getting floor map projects only, with no frontend change.
  • PATCH cannot change the type (it ignores keys it does not know), and a duplicate keeps its source's type.

Migration: applied to the database on 2026-10-02, before the merge. All 613 existing projects read floormap.

Tests: src/routes/v1/project_type_test.go, 7 tests through the real routes. Ten mutation checks each turn a test red.

Checked on production (192.168.1.226): the new build is running (GET /v1/live/:key answers projectType: "floormap"). The list and recent queries were run read-only on the database as the new build sends them: the account with the most projects gets its 45 floor maps and 4 recent ones. Not checked: the dashboard itself in a browser.

Released to main (4ab6d15, PR #210) on 2026-10-02.

Commit: 7473e22

issues.display_title: Issue #205: Blue Line Map: keep a project's tours and serve them on the share link
issues.main_description_html:
Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

PRD: GoThruMedia/gothru-3d-floormap#1156 (Blue Line Map). PM decisions: GoThruMedia/gothru-3d-floormap#1157 (answers 2, 3 and 7). Builds on #204 (project type).

Problem

A Blue Line Map project holds GoThru Blue Line tours. The PM decided the project keeps a copy of each tour (name, key, thumbnail, panorama count and lines): the public map shows that copy, because a visitor has no GoThru connection to read tours with.

The API has nowhere to keep it. Project data is stored column by column and unknown keys are dropped, the public read (GET /v1/live/:key) returns the floor plan only, and a project's thumbnail comes from its floor images.

Scope

⚠️ API contract change and ⚠️ two new columns: run the migration before this is merged, as for #204.

  1. Columns on projects: blue_line_tours TEXT (the tours, a JSON array) and blue_line_thumbnail VARCHAR(1024) NOT NULL DEFAULT ''.
  2. PATCH /v1/projects/:id accepts blueLineTours: a JSON array sent as a string, the way canvasData is. The frontend owns the shape of a tour; the API stores the array as sent.
    • The project is not a blue_line_map → 400.
    • Not a JSON array of objects → 400. Longer than 10 MB → 413.
    • blue_line_thumbnail becomes the first tour's thumbnail when that is an https:// URL, otherwise empty. An empty array clears it.
  3. GET /v1/floorplan/:id and GET /v1/live/:key return projectType and blueLineTours ([] when there are none). Their gates do not change: a draft is for members only; a visitor reads a published project that is public, or secured with a grant.
  4. Project payloads (create, list, recent, get, update, duplicate): for a Blue Line Map, thumbnail_url is blue_line_thumbnail.
  5. Duplicate keeps the tours and the thumbnail.

A tour as the frontend will send it, for reference (the API reads thumbnail only):

{ "mid": 123, "tourKey": "wRFfuWce", "name": "Cidahu", "thumbnail": "https://img.gothru.org/…", "panoramaCount": 5, "lines": [[106.71, -6.78, 106.72, -6.79]] }

Acceptance criteria

  • PATCH blueLineTours on a Blue Line Map stores the array; GET /v1/floorplan/:id returns it with projectType: "blue_line_map".
  • PATCH blueLineTours on a floor map project → 400, nothing stored.
  • Not an array, or an element that is not an object → 400, and the stored tours are unchanged.
  • thumbnail_url in list, recent and get is the first tour's thumbnail. Removing every tour clears it. A thumbnail that is not https:// is ignored.
  • Published Blue Line Map: GET /v1/live/:key returns the tours to a visitor. Private → 403. Secured without a grant → 401, with no tours in the body.
  • A draft's tours are not readable by someone who is not a member.
  • Duplicate keeps the tours and the thumbnail.
  • A floor map project answers as before, plus projectType: "floormap" and blueLineTours: [].
  • go test ./... passes.

FE counterpart: the Blue Line Map editor and public map tasks on GoThruMedia/gothru-3d-floormap, created when the design arrives (#1157 answer 5).

RESULT

Implemented and merged to development (8e2330c, PR #208) on 2026-10-02. go build ./..., go vet ./... and go test ./... pass.

What changed

  • src/models/models.go: Project.BlueLineTours (blue_line_tours TEXT) and Project.BlueLineThumbnail (blue_line_thumbnail VARCHAR(1024) NOT NULL DEFAULT '').
  • src/action/v1/project/update.go: PATCH accepts blueLineTours, a JSON array sent as a string.
  • src/action/v1/project/shared.go: blueLineThumbnail (shape check + the first tour's thumbnail), thumbnailURL, the 10 MB cap.
  • src/action/v1/floorplan/shared.go: GET /v1/floorplan/:id and GET /v1/live/:key return projectType and blueLineTours.
  • migrations/202610020002_add_blue_line_tours_to_projects.sql.

Rules as built

  • blueLineTours on a project that is not a blue_line_map, or not sent as a string → 400. Not a JSON array of objects → 400. More than 10 MB → 413. A refused PATCH leaves the stored tours as they were.
  • The API stores the array as sent and reads only the first tour's thumbnail: kept when it is an https:// URL of at most 1024 characters, otherwise empty. It is the project's thumbnail_url.
  • The read gates did not change: a draft is for members only, a private project answers 403 and a locked one 401, neither with tours in the body.
  • The tours are passed through as stored, without decoding them on every read. A row that holds invalid JSON reads as [].
  • Duplicate keeps the tours and the thumbnail.

Migration: applied to the database on 2026-10-02, before the merge.

Tests: src/routes/v1/blue_line_tours_test.go (8 tests through the real routes) and src/action/v1/project/blue_line_tours_test.go (the size cap). Sixteen mutation checks each turn a test red.

Checked on production (192.168.1.226): a published floor map project still opens and its answer now carries projectType: "floormap" and blueLineTours: []. Not checked: saving and reading real tours, which needs the frontend editor or a session.

Released to main (4ab6d15, PR #210) on 2026-10-02.

Commit: 665f0eb

issues.display_title: Issue #206: Switch GoThru account: replace the connected account in one step
issues.main_description_html:
Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

PRD: GoThruMedia/gothru-3d-floormap#1156 (R31, Switch GoThru Account). PM decision: GoThruMedia/gothru-3d-floormap#1157 answer 4. Follow-up to #201.

Problem

The Add Tour flow of a Blue Line Map gets a Switch GoThru Account action.

Today a user connected to GoThru account A who connects account B is refused with 409 gothru_already_connected. They have to disconnect first, and if the second connect then fails or is cancelled, they are left with no connection at all.

Decision (#1157 answer 4)

Switch replaces the connection in one step, once the new account is confirmed. The rules from GoThruMedia/gothru-3d-floormap#1151 stay: one GoThru account per MapThru account, and a GoThru account connected to another MapThru account is refused. An account that signs in to MapThru with GoThru cannot switch.

Scope

⚠️ API contract change: one new endpoint. No migration.

PUT /v1/gothru/connection, body { "access_token": "<Keycloak access token>" }

The token is verified exactly as POST /v1/gothru/connection does. Then:

  • (realm, sub) linked to another user → 409 gothru_account_in_use. Nothing changes.
  • linked to the caller → the GoThru token is refreshed, as POST does.
  • the caller has no link → the link is created, as POST does.
  • the caller is linked to a different account → the link is replaced by the new account, and the old account's stored GoThru token goes with it.
    • 409 gothru_sign_in_only when the caller has no password and an unverified email, the rule DELETE already has: GoThru is how that account signs in.

Then the GoThru token exchange. If it fails → 502, and the previous connection is back exactly as it was, its token included.

→ 200 { "connected": true, "email": "…" }

POST /v1/gothru/connection stays as it is and still answers 409 gothru_already_connected.

Acceptance criteria

  • Connected to A, PUT with B → the link is B's, the stored token is B's, and GET reports B's email.
  • B is linked to another user → 409 gothru_account_in_use; both links are unchanged.
  • PUT with the account already connected refreshes its token.
  • PUT with no connection connects.
  • A failed exchange during a replace → 502; the link is A's again, with A's token.
  • A passwordless user with an unverified email → 409 gothru_sign_in_only; the link is unchanged.
  • After a switch, account A is free: another user can connect it.
  • 401 without a session.
  • go test ./... passes.

FE counterpart: the Add Tour task on GoThruMedia/gothru-3d-floormap, created when the design arrives (#1157 answer 5).

RESULT

Implemented and merged to development (8728456, PR #209) on 2026-10-02. go build ./..., go vet ./... and go test ./... pass.

What changed

  • src/action/v1/auth/gothru_connection.go: SwitchGothru. It shares connectGothru with ConnectGothru; the sign-in-only rule moved into signsInAnotherWay, which Disconnect uses too.
  • src/controllers/v1/gothru/gothru.go, src/routes/v1/gothru.go: PUT /v1/gothru/connection, behind middleware.Auth(). No migration.

Rules as built

  • The GoThru account is linked to another user → 409 gothru_account_in_use. The account the caller already has → its token is refreshed. No link → the link is created.
  • The caller has another account → the same link row takes the new account, and the old account's stored GoThru token is wiped with it.
  • That replace is refused with 409 gothru_sign_in_only for a user with no password and an unverified email.
  • A failed GoThru exchange → 502, and the previous connection is back as it was, token included. The same happens when the exchange stores no token.
  • POST /v1/gothru/connection is unchanged: a second account still answers 409 gothru_already_connected.

Tests: src/action/v1/auth/gothru_switch_test.go (8 tests) and gothru_switch_route_test.go (POST refuses and PUT replaces, through the real routes). Twelve mutation checks each turn a test red.

Not verified: the real flow through Keycloak and the GoThru API. From outside, without a session, the new route cannot be told apart from the old build (the /v1/gothru group answers 401 either way).

Released to main (4ab6d15, PR #210) on 2026-10-02.

Commit: 7a25901

issues.display_title: Issue #211: Remove the unused Blue Line save endpoint PUT /v1/gothru/tours/:mid/panoramas
issues.main_description_html:
Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

PRD: GoThruMedia/gothru-3d-floormap#1156 (Non-goals 1 and 3: the GoThru tour is not edited, panoramas are not moved). PM decision: GoThruMedia/gothru-3d-floormap#1157 answer 1 (the old Blue Line placement editors are removed). Follow-up to #195 and #198.

Problem

PUT /v1/gothru/tours/:mid/panoramas (#195, hardened in #198) writes panorama positions into GoThru through PUT /v1/internal/panoramas/locations/batch, signed with INTERNAL_API_KEY.

Its only caller was the Blue Line placement editor, which GoThruMedia/gothru-3d-floormap#1163 removed (commit 1b2cf88c, released to main 6e355c52 on 2026-10-05). Blue Line Map now stores its own copy of each tour in projects.blue_line_tours (#205) and never writes to GoThru.

The endpoint still runs in production. Any signed-in user with a GoThru connection can still move the panoramas of their own tours through it, which the product no longer allows, and the Floormap API keeps a key that writes to GoThru's internal endpoints for nothing.

Scope

⚠️ API contract change: one endpoint is removed. No migration. No frontend change: nothing in the frontend calls it (checked at cb753cc0).

Remove:

  • src/routes/v1/gothru.go:18: the PUT /tours/:mid/panoramas route.
  • src/controllers/v1/gothru/gothru.go:23: UpdatePanoramas.
  • src/action/v1/gothru/proxy.go:251-406: UpdatePanoramasRequest, ownTourKey and UpdatePanoramas.
  • src/action/v1/gothru/token.go:37-38: internalAPIKey(). UpdatePanoramas is its only reader.
